subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Dunning-Kruger Effect
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Dunning-Kruger Effect.

hook.text: A bank robber covered his face in lemon juice believing it would make him invisible to cameras.

buildup.text: Dunning and Kruger found that the least competent people consistently overestimate their own ability.

discovery.text: The same skills needed to be good at something are needed to evaluate how good you are at it.

twist.text: Experts tend to underestimate themselves. They assume others find it equally easy and discount their own skill.

climax.text: Seek external feedback to calibrate your self-assessment. Your own view is structurally unreliable.

punchline.text: If you feel certain, seek feedback. Certainty hides gaps.

quiz.question: Why do less competent people overestimate their abilities?
options: They are naturally more confident than experts
They lack the skills needed to recognize their own incompetence
They receive more positive feedback from colleagues
